source_extracts.label: Ohio BMV — How to Title (used vehicle, paper title)
source_extracts.quote: The seller must complete the “assignment of ownership” portion on the back of the title and have their signature(s) notarized. Then present it to the buyer to finalize the transfer.

source_extracts.label: Ohio BMV — How to Title (30-day rule)
source_extracts.quote: Title transfers must take place within 30 days of the date of sale, otherwise a late fee will be assessed.

source_extracts.label: Ohio BMV — How to Title (electronic title, BMV 3770)
source_extracts.quote: Seller – Completes page 1 of the BMV 3770 in its entirety and has their signature(s) notarized. All owners must complete the assignment.

source_extracts.label: Ohio BMV — How to Title (what to bring to title office)
source_extracts.quote: Original title assigned to the buyer; Acceptable identification; For out-of-state titles only, an out-of-state vehicle identification number (VIN) inspection; Sales tax on the purchase price; Payment for title fees, including a lien holder notation (if applicable)

source_extracts.label: Ohio BMV — Title Fees
source_extracts.quote: The $18 title fee applies statewide. In some counties, the fee may be $23 if local officials approve an additional charge.

source_extracts.label: Ohio BMV — Out-of-State Vehicle Inspection fee
Ohio BMV — Other Fees, Notary Public Fee
Ohio Revised Code 147.08 — notary fee cap
source_extracts.quote: (1) Up to five dollars for any notarial act that is not an online notarization;

source_extracts.label: ORC 4505.063 — dealer exception (HB 567, eff. April 6, 2023)
source_extracts.quote: when a motor vehicle dealer licensed under Chapter 4517. of the Revised Code is a party to the transfer of a motor vehicle, no notarization is required on a motor vehicle certificate of title, an application for a motor vehicle certificate of title, assignment of ownership to the motor vehicle

source_extracts.label: Ohio Secretary of State — Notary FAQ (ID validity)
source_extracts.quote: Inspect an acceptable government-issued ID (passport, driver license, or government-issued ID with a photo or signature). ID must be current or not expired for more than 3 years.

source_extracts.label: Ohio BMV — How to Title (titles issued by clerks, not BMV)
source_extracts.quote: Ohio titles are issued by Clerk of Courts title offices, the BMV does not issue titles.

source_extracts.label: Mailbox Plus notary service page (store's own fee, from siteConfig)
source_extracts.quote: $5 per signature, as set by Ohio state law. No membership required. ... certified notary is on staff during all business hours. Walk in with your unsigned document and a valid ID.

scope_rules.forbidden: claiming the buyer's signature must be notarized on a paper-title assignment
scope_rules.reason: BMV page requires the SELLER's signature(s) notarized on the assignment of ownership; buyer then finalizes the transfer at the title office

scope_rules.forbidden: claiming notarization is no longer required in Ohio (blanket)
scope_rules.reason: ORC 4505.063 waives notarization ONLY when a licensed dealer is a party to the transfer; private casual sales still require the seller's notarized assignment

scope_rules.forbidden: stating the exact late-fee dollar amount
scope_rules.reason: BMV page says 'a late fee will be assessed' without an amount on the fetched page; do not invent a figure

scope_rules.forbidden: listing a specific county title-office address or hours
scope_rules.reason: titles are issued by county Clerk of Courts offices; address not verified in this run — point readers to the BMV county office search

scope_rules.forbidden: 'works on every form' or categorical acceptance claims
per-signature pricing arithmetic implying multi-signer totals beyond the $5 cap
scope_rules.reason: ORC 147.08(C): fees shall not be calculated on a per-signature basis by the notary; the store's published price is $5 per signature — do not construct scenarios beyond it

required_when.claim: the seller's signature must be notarized
required_when.qualifier: on a paper title assignment of ownership for a private (non-dealer) sale

required_when.claim: buyer does not have to be present at the notarization
required_when.qualifier: only the seller signs before the notary on the assignment; the buyer completes the transfer at the Clerk of Courts title office — frame as what the BMV instructions require, not a legal guarantee for every edge case
